The side AB is labeled 14 and the side AC is labeled 19. Segment AN is drawn from A toward the interior, with N on AN, and BN is drawn perpendicular to AN as indicated by the right-angle mark. Reasoning: Since AN bisects angle BAC, reflecting point B across line AN sends ray AB onto ray AC. Let the reflection of B be B'. Then B' lies on AC and AB' = AB = 14. Because AC = 19, the remaining length B'C is 19 - 14 = 5. Also, since B' is the reflection of B across AN, line AN is the perpendicular bisector of BB', so N is the midpoint of BB'. Given that M is the midpoint of BC, in triangle BCB', segment MN joins the midpoints of BB' and BC. By the midpoint theorem, MN = B'C/2 = 5/2.

method.method_draft: Use a reflection-midpoint argument. From the diagram/text, note that AN is the angle bisector and BN is perpendicular to AN, with N on AN. Reflect point B across line AN to a point B'. Because AN bisects angle BAC, the reflected ray AB lies along ray AC, so B' lies on AC and AB' = AB = 14. Since AC = 19, the remaining segment B'C has length 19 - 14 = 5. Also, because AN is the perpendicular bisector of BB', N is the midpoint of BB'. M is given as the midpoint of BC. In triangle BCB', segment MN joins the midpoints of BB' and BC, so by the midpoint theorem MN is parallel to B'C and MN = B'C/2 = 5/2.

method.method_draft: Use coordinates with the angle bisector as an axis. Place A at the origin and let AN be the x-axis. Since AN bisects angle BAC, choose the rays AB and AC to make equal opposite angles with the x-axis: let B = (14 cos t, 14 sin t) and C = (19 cos t, -19 sin t), where t = theta/2. Because BN is perpendicular to AN, N is the projection of B onto the x-axis, so N = (14 cos t, 0). Since M is the midpoint of BC, M = ((14 cos t + 19 cos t)/2, (14 sin t - 19 sin t)/2). Then compute vector MN = M - N = ((5/2) cos t, -(5/2) sin t), whose length is sqrt((5/2)^2 cos^2 t + (5/2)^2 sin^2 t) = 5/2.
